topic: Generator concurrency of 1024 at 1000 requests per second

setup.host_interference: The user reported a simultaneous video call after the run. The call may have contributed to host contention. No per-application measurement establishes its contribution.
setup.repeat: Deferred after the user reported the call. Docker Desktop was not restarted. Development services were restored.

checks.review_scope: Generator concurrency limit and its README documentation.

report.storage: local Docker named volume; loopback HTTP; no TLS or artificial network delay
limitations: Short probes identify candidate rates, not sustained or 30-day capacity.
Shared host workloads may affect results; no other containers are stopped.
SDK events and adapter wire output are recorded once, then replayed with new identities.
Verification retains compact replay descriptions; complete expected payloads are reconstructed and compared after restart.
OTLP batching and gzip model a gateway; SDK adapters still send one event per request.
Request latency starts after serialization/compression; preparation and schedule lag are reported separately.
Resource sampling includes Docker exec overhead and may miss peaks. Container memory includes filesystem cache.
Scheduled retention scans run every five seconds with a 30-day TTL; these runs do not measure deletion of expired data.

Optional aggregate profiling covers the process lifetime, including preload, health checks and startup retention, but excludes schema initialization and final checkpoint. It is unavailable after SIGKILL. Queue depth and internal timing percentiles are not measured.
Image ID identifies the executable. Git source provenance is the local checkout and cannot attest to a separately supplied image.

local_test_setup.note: Development services were stopped externally. The collector image and workload implementation are unchanged from the compact-ledger comparison. The generator concurrency rises from 512 to 1024. Memory, disk, unique-event and latency guards are unchanged.

summary.note: Cumulative host-wide page activity during setup, traffic and verification. Compression totals can exceed physical RAM because the same pages can be processed repeatedly. These counters do not identify a responsible application.
